summary.text: Brian Jack is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 3rd Congressional District, first elected in 2024. He previously worked on Donald Trump's 2016 and 2024 presidential campaigns, and his official biography says he served as White House Political Director during the first Trump administration. He is seeking re-election.

paragraphs.text: According to his campaign website, Jack is a sixth-generation Georgian who was raised in Fayette County and graduated from Woodward Academy; his official biography lists him as a resident of Peachtree City.
He earned a bachelor's degree from Pepperdine University in 2010.
After college he worked in conservative advocacy, according to his campaign website, including for Dr. Ben Carson and on efforts to strengthen the United States-Israel relationship.
Jack joined Donald Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and served as its national delegate management director ahead of the Republican National Convention.

His official biography says he was one of President Trump's longest-serving aides and served as White House Political Director during the first Trump administration, then worked as a liaison between congressional Republicans and Trump.
He later served as a senior advisor to Trump's 2024 presidential campaign.
Jack won the 2024 Republican primary runoff against Mike Dugan on June 18, 2024, and the November 2024 general election against Democrat Maura Keller, 66.3% to 33.7%.

In the 2025-2026 term he serves on the House Committees on Oversight and Government Reform, Rules, and Small Business, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Innovation, Entrepreneurship, and Workforce Development.
He is a member of the Georgia Historical Society, the Fayette County Historical Society, and the Sons of the American Revolution.
